title: ANY Operator
description: Learn how to use the SQL Server ANY operator to compare a value with a set of values returned by a subquery.

data.text: The ANY operator is a logical operator that compares a scalar value with a single-column set of values returned by a subquery. It returns TRUE if any comparison between the scalar value and a value from the subquery result evaluates to TRUE.

data.title: ANY Operator Syntax
data.content: Compares a scalar expression against each value returned by the subquery.

data.text: In this syntax, the subquery must return a single column with a data type compatible with the scalar expression. The ANY operator returns TRUE if at least one comparison pair evaluates to TRUE.

data.title: Note
data.text: The SOME operator is equivalent to the ANY operator and can be used interchangeably.
The following query finds products that were sold with more than two units in any sales order.

data.title: ANY with Product Filter
data.content: Finds products sold in quantities of two or more in any order.
data.code:
SELECT
    product_name,
    list_price
FROM
    production.products
WHERE
    product_id = ANY (
        SELECT
            product_id
        FROM
            sales.order_items
        WHERE
            quantity >= 2
    )
ORDER BY
    product_name;

data.title: ANY Operator Key Points
points: ANY compares a scalar value against each value in a subquery result set.
Returns TRUE if any comparison evaluates to TRUE.
The SOME operator is a synonym for ANY.
The subquery must return a single column.
